sources.note: Kepo' appears only in comparative sound-correspondence tables (data credited to Nggidung 2020, unpublished Kepoq wordlist) and in the classification tree sec. 3.4 p.164 ('Kepo\' [kuk] *-ay > a; **z > r'). Only an areal generalisation in sec. 3.2.1.2 'Schwa' (Flores phonology), printed p.115: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.'
